title: Microsoft Edge: automatically unsubscribe users from notifications sent by scam and malicious sites
summary: The briefing passes: the current Microsoft release notes and roadmap support the automatic protection, restoration route and existing notification controls. All cited Learn pages opened successfully despite the pre-check's throttling errors; the November 25 update does not change this feature. The impact rating needs a minor correction because this protection changes notification behaviour automatically.

claims.claim: The feature belongs to Microsoft Edge version 158.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge: v.158 - Automatically unsubscribe users from notifications sent by scam and malicious sites

claims.claim: The described trigger is a notification leading users to a site SmartScreen blocks as a scam, phishing or malware page.

claims.quote: Set whether websites can display desktop notifications. You can allow them by default ('AllowNotifications'), deny them by default ('BlockNotifications'), or have the user be asked each time a website wants to show a notification ('AskNotifications').

claims.claim: A low impact rating fits this automatic change to existing notification behaviour.
claims.quote: impact: low; defaultState: on. The standard defines low as admins only or a small opt-in group, and high as most users or a change to default behaviour.
claims.fix: Set impact to high. Replace the impact rationale with: "High. Edge changes notification behaviour automatically when a notification leads to a SmartScreen-blocked scam, phishing or malware page; affected users do not opt in to this protection."
